title: Compliance Memorandum — Lease Term Agreement Rent Changes and Increase Notice
content:
A rent change on a Lease Term Agreement is recorded when a renewal, transfer or month-to-month conversion term starts, and when the rent of a month-to-month agreement is adjusted; the rent of a fixed term never changes mid-term.

## 1. Which changes need notice

1.1 A signed renewal or transfer is the resident's agreement to its rent and needs no advance notice.

1.2 For a month-to-month conversion or adjustment that raises the rent, the required notice is the longer of the company minimum notice of the Month-to-Month Agreement (30 calendar days) and the notice days for the community's state below, where the California figure for an increase above ten percent over the prior twelve months is the over-threshold one.

| Community state | Notice days, standard | Notice days, over threshold |
|---|---|---|
| California | 30 | 90 |
| Washington | 90 | 90 |
| Colorado | 60 | 60 |
| Texas | 0 | 0 |
| Georgia | 0 | 0 |
| Arizona | 0 | 0 |

## 2. When a noticed rent may take effect

2.1 **Notice matured.** For a month-to-month conversion or adjustment, a new rent may take effect only when the current date is later than the date the rent change notice was delivered plus the required notice days. Notice days are counted as calendar days starting the day after delivery, and the new rent may take effect on the day after the last notice day at the earliest. The delivery date is the notice date on the rent change record.

2.2 When the notice given was shorter, the previous rent continues and the rent change takes effect on the first day the notice allows.

2.3 No increase may make the rent exceed the previous rent by more than the statutory increase cap of the renewal offer rule — 8.8 percent in California and 9.68 percent in Washington — over any twelve months in a state that has one.

## 3. Worked cases (hypothetical dates and rents)

| Case | Required notice | Last notice day | Earliest effective date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Month-to-month increase in Colorado, notice delivered 1 March | longer of 30 and 60, so 60 days | 30 April | 1 May |
| Month-to-month increase in Texas, notice delivered 1 March | longer of 30 and 0, so 30 days | 31 March | 1 April |
| Month-to-month increase in California of 12 percent over the prior twelve months, notice delivered 1 March | longer of 30 and 90, so 90 days | 30 May | 31 May |

In the Colorado case a new rent dated 30 April may not take effect — 30 April is the last notice day, not later than it; the previous rent continues through 30 April and the change takes effect on 1 May.
